youtube_video.title: Unleashed vs Katana for Small Manufacturers in Australia and NZ
youtube_video.description:
Read the full comparison: https://zudoworks.com/insights/unleashed-vs-katana/

Unleashed and Katana are two of the first names a small maker in Australia or New Zealand meets after outgrowing spreadsheets. Both run in a browser, both track stock and purchase orders, and both connect to Xero. In daily use they lean in different directions. This 50-second explainer sets out the differences, read from both vendors' own pricing, feature and help pages on 26 November 2026.

Chapters
00:00 Unleashed or Katana?
00:04 Unleashed: stock first
00:10 Katana: production first
00:15 Production is a module in Unleashed
00:20 How Unleashed charges
00:26 Katana's free plan and Advantage
00:31 Xero, QuickBooks Online and MYOB
00:37 Which one fits your shop
00:42 Read the full comparison

Key facts
- Unleashed was founded in Auckland in 2009 and is inventory software first: stock across warehouses, wholesale and trade customers, and sales channels such as Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon and eBay.
- Katana puts production nearer the centre: manufacturing orders that reserve materials, routing steps, planned against actual cost, and a Shop Floor App for operators.
- In Unleashed, bills of materials and assemblies are not supported on the Lite package. Production comes with Pro, or as an add-on to Core.
- Unleashed is sold as three packages, Lite, Core and Pro, each with allowances of users and sales orders, plus paid extras and optional modules.
- Katana has a Free plan of up to 30 SKUs with unlimited users, then Advantage: one custom annual price that is not per user. Raw materials and packaging count as SKUs.
- Both connect to Xero and QuickBooks Online. Neither has a native MYOB connection; a third-party app links Unleashed to MYOB AccountRight.

Which one fits? If stock, channels and trade customers are your hard part, look at Unleashed. If several operations, operators on the floor and make-to-order work are your hard part, look at Katana. If you quote every job to a customer drawing, neither is built around that.

Before you sign up: count your SKUs, count your users and monthly orders, and run a mock recall in the trial.

Plans and features change, so check both vendors' pages before you decide. We do not quote other vendors' prices.

Zudo Works builds manufacturing and business software for small manufacturers. More guides: https://zudoworks.com/insights/

linkedin_profile_video:
When a maker in Auckland or Melbourne asks me "Unleashed or Katana?", I answer with a question: where is your hard part?

Both products run in a browser, track stock and purchase orders, and connect to Xero. So on a shortlist they look like twins. In daily use, they are not.

Unleashed grew up around stock. Several warehouses, hundreds of trade accounts, orders arriving from Shopify, Amazon and eBay. Production is there, but as a module, and it isn't on the Lite package at all.

Katana grew up around the workshop. A manufacturing order reserves the materials, moves through the steps you define, and shows planned against actual cost. Operators tick off their tasks in a Shop Floor App.

Two details I'd check before signing either:

→ Count every SKU, raw materials and packaging included. Katana's free plan stops at 30, and most real makers pass that quickly.
→ Ask how your accounts will connect. Both link to Xero and QuickBooks Online. Neither has a native MYOB link.

And one test I'd always run in the trial: a mock recall. Take one raw material batch and see if the system shows every customer it reached, in one report.

We make our own manufacturing software, ZMOS, so I have an interest. The guide says plainly where both of these are the better choice.

The number I'd write down first when comparing Unleashed and Katana: your SKU count.

Not finished products. Every item you track. Raw materials, packaging, components and finished goods.

Here's why it matters. Katana's free plan covers up to 30 SKUs with unlimited users. Past that, it's one custom annual price, and it isn't per user. Unleashed works differently: Lite, Core or Pro, each with a set number of users and sales orders a month, plus extras you add.

So the same business can look cheap on one and expensive on the other, depending on whether it has many SKUs, many users or many orders.

Then the second question: what is your hard part?

→ Stock across warehouses, trade customers, online channels: Unleashed is built for that.
→ Several operations per product and people reporting from the floor: Katana goes further.
→ Every job quoted to a customer drawing: neither, honestly.

I put the comparison into four slides, read from both vendors' own pages.
